title: Assessing human iPSC-derived microglia identity and function by immunostaining, phagocytosis, calcium activity, and inflammation assay
protocol: Seed collected microglia cells as described in "before you begin".
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2, overnight (∼15–17 h).
Prepare the solutions of formaldehyde solution, blocking solution, and antibody solution.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add 200 μL PBS per well to wash the cells.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 200 μL of 4% (w/v) formaldehyde solution at room temperature per well.
Incubate cells for 15 min in the fixative at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Collect the formaldehyde solution and dispose it in the aldehyde waste disposal.
Add 200 μL PBS per well.
Incubate cells for 5 min in PBS.
Aspirate PBS.
Repeat steps adding 200 μL PBS, incubating for 5 min, and aspirating PBS a total of three times.
Stain fixed cells by incubating them in 150 μL blocking solution for two hours at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Prepare the primary antibodies in diluting the desired antibody concentration in 150 μL antibody solution per well.
Mix 0.6 μL goat-anti-IBA1 and 1.5 μL rabbit-anti-P2Y12 to get a 1:250 and 1:100 dilution, respectively, for Well 1.
Mix 0.6 μL goat-anti-IBA1 and 0.3 μL rabbit-anti-PU.1 to get a 1:250 and 1:500 dilution, respectively, for Well 2.
Aspirate the blocking solution.
Add the antibody solution containing the desired primary antibodies.
Incubate the plate overnight (∼15–17 h) at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Transfer the plate to 4°C to prevent denaturation of reagents and evaporation of the solution.
Aspirate the antibody solution.
Perform the washing step described in steps 2g–j.
Prepare a total of 300 μL antibody solution by adding 0.15 μL goat-anti-Alexa Fluor 488 and 0.15 μL rabbit-anti-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:2000 dilution).
Add 150 μL of the secondary antibodies containing antibody solution into each well.
Incubate the cells light-protected for 2 h at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Aspirate the antibody solution.
Perform the washing step described in steps 2g–j.
Dilute 0.1 μL Hoechst 33342 (1:5000) in 500 μL PBS to obtain a Hoechst-PBS solution.
Add 200 μL of the diluted Hoechst-PBS solution per well.
Incubate the cells light-protected for 8 min.
Perform the washing step described in steps 2g–j.
Place the Ibidi-chamber into the specimen holder of the microscope.
Use a 20× objective to find the region-of-interest and determine whether the cells expressed the investigated marker.
Use a 40× oil immersion objective to focus on a small subset of microglia to investigate expression details.
Drag microscope images into the Imaris File Converter.
Press “Start all” in the Imaris File Converter.
Open converted files in Imaris.
Open “Display Adjustment” to visualize individual image channels.
Process images if necessary by clicking the “Image Processing” icon on the toolbar.
Select median filter from the dropdown box of each channel.
Apply background subtraction for each channel and press “OK”.
Visualize the channel or channels of interest.
Select the icon “Snapshot”.
Seed collected microglia cells as described in “before you begin” – seeding cells.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight (∼15–17 h).
Preheat the microscope chamber to 37°C.
Set up the microscope using a 20× air objective.
Activate the 488 nm and 568 nm laser channels simultaneously to limit bleed-through.
Set up a time series imaging for 1 cycle per minute over 80 cycles total.
Activate the z-stack option during imaging.
Enable autofocus for each cycle to compensate for drifting on the z-axis.
Prepare lectin staining solution by adding 0.2 μL tomato-lectin to 200 μL DPBS.
Pre-warm DPBS, lectin staining solution, and Leibovitz’s L-15 medium to 37°C in a bead bath.
Aspirate the medium from the Ibidi-chamber.
Wash cells with 200 μL pre-warmed DPBS.
Aspirate DPBS.
Add 200 μL of lectin staining solution to the cells.
Transfer cells for 20 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Before imaging, aspirate the lectin staining solution.
Wash cells with 200 μL DPBS.
Add 390 μL pre-warmed Leibovitz’s L-15 medium.
Protect stained cells from light and transfer them to the microscope.
Place the Ibidi-chamber into the specimen holder.
Select a representative region-of-interest for imaging.
Set a z-stack to acquire the entire volume of the microglia-like cells.
Remove the lid of the Ibidi-chamber before starting the time series.
Start recording.
Acquire 20 min of baseline.
Re-suspend beads at 1 mg/mL in pre-warmed Leibovitz’s L-15 medium according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Sonicate beads for 30 s at room temperature (20°C–22°C) to homogenously disperse particles shortly before use.
Immediately add 10 μL of freshly sonicated beads in Leibovitz’s L-15 medium to the Ibidi-chamber without stopping the recording.
Keep recording for the remaining 60 minutes to image the bead uptake.
Repeat the assay three times from three independent differentiations.
Access Imaris and obtain a license.
Obtain access to R software.
Process images by applying “Median Filter” and “Background Subtraction (local contrast)” to both channels.
Visualize the microglia channel.
Click the icon “Surface rendering” to create a new surface.
Press the blue icon for “Next” in the newly opened window.
Create the surface of microglia.
Select the channel that labels microglia in the “Source channel” option.
Enter the surface detail resolution, keeping it consistent across the experiment.
Press the blue icon for “Next”.
Adjust the threshold with the slider to visualize microglia surface and minimize background.
Use the microglia channel as a reference.
Press the green button for “Finish”.
Open the statistics of the created surfaces.
Select the newly generated “Surface 1” tab.
Select the “Statistics” icon.
Select “Detailed”.
Select “Average Values”.
Select “Intensity Mean Ch=2 Img=1”.
Select the icon “Export data for plotting” and export data as .xlsx.
Seed collected microglia cells as described in the protocol for seeding cells.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight (∼15–17 h).
Reconstitute Fluo-4 Ca2+-assay solution according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Pre-warm 550 μL of Fluo-4 Ca2+-assay solution to 37°C in a bead bath.
Aliquot reconstituted Fluo-4 Ca2+-assay solution and store at -20°C for up to 2 weeks.
Prepare 200 μL of 10 mM ATP in Leibovitz’s L-15 medium.
Label attached microglia-like cells with the 1× Fluo-4 Ca2+-assay solution.
Aspirate the medium from labeled cells.
Add 250 μL of 1× Fluo-4 Ca2+-assay solution per well.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Remove cells from incubator and protect them from light.
Incubate cells at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for another 30 min.
Aspirate the 1× Fluo-4 Ca2+-assay solution.
Add 270 μL of pre-warmed Leibovitz’s L-15 medium to each well.
Set up microscope and image calcium activity.
Place Ibidi-chamber into specimen holder.
Activate the 488 nm laser channel.
Use a 20× air objective for imaging.
Select an area with around 50 cells per field-of-view.
Set a time series with 1 cycle/500 ms and total recording time of 360 s.
Remove lid of Ibidi-chamber before starting acquisition.
Record 180 s/360 frames of baseline activity.
Add 30 μL of ATP in Leibovitz’s L-15 medium to the well for a final concentration of 1 mM.
Continue acquisition for an additional 180 s.
Reduce laser power and gain to minimize photo bleaching.
Use 0.5% laser power of a 25 mW Argon-Multiline laser and a gain of 500.
Remove the lid before starting the acquisition to prevent loss of region-of-interest.
Pipette ATP solution carefully onto the surface of the medium without disturbing it.
Do not re-suspend the medium while adding ATP.
Repeat steps for obtaining baseline activity in a second well as control.
Add Leibovitz’s L-15 medium instead of ATP at step 35h for the control.
Perform the assay three times from three independent differentiations.
Select the “Input” directory for files to be run in batch.
Define where the processed files will be saved by selecting an “Output” directory.
Press the “Convert” icon to start processing the files.
Record and create the macro code for batch conversion.
Load an image by pressing “File” and then “Open.”
Select “Plugins,” followed by “Macros,” and choose “Record.”
The “Recorder” window appears; apply a Gaussian Blur to the image.
Adjust the parameters for the Gaussian Blur, setting the sigma (radius) as needed.
Preview the image before starting the processing.
Confirm with “OK” to start the blur process.
Apply a look-up-table (LUT) to the images by selecting “LUT.”
Choose one of the listed options for LUT application.
Save the macro code in the “Recorder” window.
Select the “Input” directory for batch processing.
Define the “Output” directory where processed files will be saved.
Insert the macro code into the empty field.
Select "Process" to start the batch processing.
Set analysis parameters.
Choose "Set measurements".
Select "Mean grey values".
Press "OK".
Open processed file and select your regions of interest (ROIs).
Go to "Tools".
Choose "ROI Manager".
Manually select ROIs using an elliptic shape centered on individual cells.
Select "Add" to have the ROI listed.
Select "Show all" and "Labels" to visualize and annotate all selected ROIs.
Repeat step for all cells of interest.
Measure the "Mean intensity levels" for each frame.
Select "More" and "Multi Measure" in the ROI manager.
Activate the two options: "Measure all slices" and "One row per slice".
Press "OK".
Export the "Mean intensity values".
Order primers for gene-of-interest.
Download RNA sequence of the gene-of-interest from NCBI.
Copy the sequence into Primer-Blast.
Set the product length to 70-200 base pairs (bp).
Choose a primer pair with lengths between 18-24 bp and G/C content between 40%-60%.
Ensure the Tm of primers is within 50°C-60°C range.
Avoid self-complementary structures shorter than 8 bp.
Prevent cross-dimer formation less than 5 bp.
Order primers for selected primer pair.
Validate primers by running a RT-qPCR on a test sample.
Check PCR product size using an agarose gel.
Run RT-qPCR on serial dilutions of the test sample to check efficiency.
Seed collected microglia cells as described in the protocol.
Adjust the culture format and cell number according to Table 2.
Incubate cells overnight at 37°C, 5% CO2 (∼15–17 h).
Pre-warm 2,000 μL of microglia medium for 4 wells.
Dilute stock solutions of inflammatory stimuli IFNy and IL-1β in microglia medium to a concentration of 10 ng/mL each.
Dilute LPS in microglia medium to a concentration of 100 ng/mL.
Dilute poly I:C in microglia medium to a concentration of 50 μg/mL.
Aspirate the medium from attached microglia-like cells.
Add 500 μL of diluted IFNy + IL-1β into well 1.
Add 500 μL of diluted LPS into well 2.
Add 500 μL of diluted poly I:C into well 3.
Add 500 μL microglia medium only (control condition) into well 4.
Incubate cells for 6 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Work on an RNAse-free bench and keep samples on ice during RNA isolation.
Clean the working area before starting RNA isolation with 20% bleach.
Aspirate supernatant from the sample plate placed on an RNAse-free bench.
Add lysis buffer as per manufacturer’s instructions for innuPREP RNA Mini Kit 2.0.
Measure RNA concentration with a Nanodrop Spectrometer after isolation.
Perform a reference measurement “blank” of the nuclease-free water used to dilute RNA samples.
Check that the A260/280 ratio is between 1.9–2.1 to assess RNA purity.
Store isolated RNA at −80°C if not proceeding immediately to cDNA synthesis.
Perform cDNA synthesis using the LunaScript RT SuperMix Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute all samples to the same concentration of input RNA for each condition within experimental repetitions.
Prepare one reaction for cDNA synthesis per sample and mix by up-and-down pipetting.
Prepare one no RT-control per biological replicate and mix by up-and-down pipetting.
Prepare a no-template control and mix by up-and-down pipetting.
Set up thermocycler according to the specified protocol.
Clean the working area with a 20% bleach solution.
Handle all procedures on ice.
Dilute primers in nuclease-free dH2O to a concentration of 1 μM.
Calculate the total volume for the appropriate number of reactions plus 10% overage.
Dilute cDNA 1:10 in nuclease-free dH2O.
Thaw ready-to-use master mix on ice.
Prepare master mix for each gene, including 4 housekeeping genes and 3 genes-of-interest without adding DNA template.
Distribute the master mix into a 384 well plate.
Add DNA samples to the plate.
Seal the plate with a thin, topically transparent film.
Spin the plate for 1 min at 500 g.
Perform quantitative real time PCR (qRT-PCR).
Program light-cycler according to table:files/protocols_protocol_2171_15.csv.
Start the light-cycler.
Select the “Second Derivate Maximum Method” to determine Cq-values after completion of the run.
Export the data as .xlsx file from Lightcycler 480 software.
Repeat the assay 3–5 times using microglia-like cells harvested from independent differentiations.
Calculate the mean Cq values from the three technical replicates for each gene.
Calculate the standard deviation for the mean Cq values for each gene.
Remove technical replicates with a standard deviation larger than 0.5.
Calculate the geometric mean of the four reference genes.
Calculate ΔCq values by normalizing mean Cq values of all genes of interest to the geometric mean of the reference genes measured within the same sample.
Calculate ΔΔCq values by normalizing ΔCq values of treated samples to untreated control within each experimental repetition.
Transform ΔΔCq values from log2-scale to describe fold changes between the treated and untreated group.
Use software R to visualize and analyze the data.
Perform one-sample t-test to compare stimulated condition with its untreated control.
Adjust for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg method.
